topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer causes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture, introduces the speaker, and outlines the core learning objectives regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer mechanisms.

topics.label: Factors driving cancer risk: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the origins of cancer by evaluating the interplay between intrinsic mutational processes, environmental exposures, inherited susceptibility, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious mechanisms in oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents such as bacteria, parasites, and oncogenic viruses drive malignancy, illustrating their mechanisms through the case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and dietary or chemical compounds undergo metabolic activation to induce direct DNA damage, reactive oxygen species, and bulky adducts.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, chronic inflammation, and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish non-mutagenic promoters from initiators, showing how chronic inflammation, signalling pathway agonists, and developmental timing create permissive environments for tumour growth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the experimental, epidemiological, and genomic approaches used to detect carcinogenic exposures and prove causality.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with framing remarks on evaluating the everyday risks and benefits of exposure to potential environmental carcinogens.
